correctness.rationale: For n>=4 the line graph L(K_n) has diameter two; a GP violation is exactly an induced P3. The chosen base edges form disjoint stars/triangles/isolates iff their line graph is P3-free. A complete proof of the star/triangle component lemma and exact labeled component counts c_1=1,c_2=z,c_3=3z^2+z^3,c_s=sz^(s-1) for s>=4 establishes the exponential generating function and recurrence, including all n=0,1,2,3 boundary cases. The number of selected edges is n minus number of nontriangle components, proving degree and maximum multiplicity. The included independent shortest-path-based verifier matches all polynomial coefficients n=0..7 and the top identities through n=20; finite checks are not used as proof.

originality.rationale: Theorem 4.4 of arXiv:1903.04286 proves the GP cardinality of L(K_n) using independent cliques and support disjointness; Theorem 5.2 of arXiv:2306.09965 proves the lower maximal size and explicitly discusses the star/triangle maximal-support structure. Those inputs are already known. Theorem 4.2 of arXiv:2401.05696 computes a full polynomial for the Kneser complement K(n,2), not the triangular graph L(K_n), and does not imply the latter because geodesics change under complement. The new explicit full generating function, recurrence and maximum-set multiplicity were not located in the materially inspected primary texts or in targeted published-finding corpus searches. Standard labeled-component enumeration may contain an algebraically identical expression not indexed as general position, which remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: A classical labeled-graph species for star forests supplemented with triangle components may have precisely this exponent outside searchable GP-poly literature.
The underlying support characterization and maximum GP number are already known and are not original contributions.
The published-finding corpus comparison used published ranked summaries; no claim of uniqueness or of unpublished-work coverage is made.

value.rationale: The graph family is classical and its maximum and smallest maximal GP set sizes were studied in 2019 and 2023. The whole ordinary GP polynomial is an invariant explicitly promoted by the 2024 literature. The new labeled EGF gives exact counts of every GP set size simultaneously, an executable root-block recurrence, and maximal-set multiplicities; these go beyond the prior one-number extrema and distinguish the full distribution. The result is a natural full-invariant classification, not an arbitrary parameter slice or a numerical increment. The standard exponential formula and prior structural lemma are credited.
